evidence: app/src/pages/ability.ts:7 — whole feature is one page file
app/src/main.ts:5,22 — one import and one route branch to delete
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:118-125 — only other reference is the Pokémon page's own Abilities section
app/index.html:16-20 — nav never links abilities, so no dead nav
app/src/style.css:201 — .card-note is generic, no ability-specific CSS to orphan
removability.rationale: Features are one page file plus a route branch; deleting Abilities touches three files and leaves no dead links or dead code. Not 5 because section markup is inlined in page templates rather than composed from named pieces.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:23 — every card list renders through pokemonCard/spriteUrl, so a sprite-URL fix covers all lists
app/src/data.ts:98-113 vs app/src/pages/ability.ts:20-38 — Pokémon→species mapping implemented twice; mapping bugs get fixed twice
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:279-305 — sort data reconstructed by scraping rendered DOM text/hrefs, duplicating column layout of moveRowHtml (:225-236)
app/src/util.ts:2-5 — manual esc() at every interpolation; new fields can silently skip escaping
changeability.rationale: The most likely fixes (card sprite, formatting, names) each land in one obvious place, but the ref→species mapping and the moves-table row model are each implemented twice, in ways that can drift apart.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:21-39 — single fetch/cache module; pages never touch fetch or URLs directly
app/src/nav.ts:9-14 — tiny bus so pages trigger navigation without importing the router
app/server.mjs:8,37-40 — server-side code fully separate; API base injected as explicit window config seam
app/src/components.ts:25 — module-global mutable sectionCounter is hidden shared state
app/src/data.ts:29 — API records cross the boundary as untyped any, weakening the seam
coupling.rationale: Clear one-way layering (api → data → components → pages → router) with narrow, explicit seams; deductions for untyped any records and one piece of global mutable state.

evidence: app/src/data.ts:15-18 — memo helper cleanly reused across seven loaders
app/src/data.ts:110-112 — speciesFromPokemonRefs hard-codes the dex sort, forcing callers wanting a different order to re-sort or fork (ability.ts did fork)
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:153-154 — section() can't take an id, so the empty-moves case hand-builds a section with a different heading-id scheme
app/src/pages/move.ts:10-16 — page skeleton (fetch/404/title) copy-pasted in types.ts, ability.ts, pokemon.ts
app/src/components.ts:18-21 — pokemonCard opts object stretches to types/note without boolean-flag creep
abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions are the right ones and stretch to most variation, but two real cases (ability's hidden flag, the moves anchor id) required forking or hand-building, and the per-resource page boilerplate is duplicated rather than generalized.

findings.issue: Moves-table sorting reconstructs MoveRow data by scraping the rendered DOM (textContent, hrefs, column offsets) instead of keeping the rows already computed in movesSectionHtml; markup changes silently break sorting.
findings.suggestion: Hand the parsed rows from movesSectionHtml to wireMovesSection (closure, WeakMap keyed by the table, or dataset) and sort that data directly.

findings.issue: Duplicates the Pokémon-ref→species mapping that speciesFromPokemonRefs (app/src/data.ts:98) already provides, differing only in tracking is_hidden; the two implementations can drift.
findings.suggestion: Generalize speciesFromPokemonRefs to also return the raw entry (or accept an extractor) and have the ability page use it.

findings.issue: SpeciesRef.id means species id in getSpeciesList (:30) but Pokémon id in speciesFromPokemonRefs (:105) and ability.ts; sprite/dex rendering only works because the spec guarantees default Pokémon ID == species ID.
findings.suggestion: Make the distinction explicit — carry species and Pokémon ids separately, or document and validate the invariant at the data boundary.

findings.issue: Default API base URL 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated in api.ts, server.mjs:8 and vite.config.ts:13.
findings.suggestion: Define the fallback in one place (e.g. a shared constant imported by server.mjs and vite.config.ts).

findings.issue: Two independent caching mechanisms (api.ts promise cache and per-helper memo) with no TTL/eviction policy seam; changing caching rules means editing both.
findings.suggestion: Fold memo into a single cache layer with a configurable policy.

findings.issue: Empty-moves case hand-builds a section with id 'moves-heading' while section() generates counter-based ids, creating two heading-id schemes for the same section.
findings.suggestion: Use section('Moves', ..., 'id="moves"') which already accepts extra attrs.

findings.issue: Fetch → isNotFound → renderNotFound → document.title boilerplate is copy-pasted in all four resource pages, raising the cost of the next Items-shaped section.
findings.suggestion: Factor a loadResourceOr404(path, root) helper returning the record or null.

findings.issue: API records flow through the app as untyped any, so data-shape changes get no compiler help and refactors rely on grep.
findings.suggestion: Declare the record shapes actually consumed (species, pokemon, type, move, ability, generation) at the data.ts boundary.

summary: A small, well-layered vanilla TS app where every scenario lands in a small, findable set of files: features are one page file plus a route branch, and card/sprite rendering has a single shared implementation. The real risks are duplicated logic (the ref→species mapping exists in two places, the moves-table row model in two places, one of which scrapes the DOM) and the untyped any records flowing across the data boundary. It's a comfortable 4: I'd merge it after fixing the DOM-reparse and the forked helper.
